answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a slow-ramp reputation ridge: every identity starts at zero weight and only climbs after a long, continuous history of attested useful work across many epochs, like copper wiring that gains value only once laid and tested. New accounts cannot buy instant influence; their votes stay violet-tinted and provisional until the ledger proves sustained, non-duplicated behavior. An attacker must fund months of genuine work per fake identity, while duplicate behavior across accounts triggers correlation checks that reset the whole cluster to zero.
